# Nose and sinuses

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Ear, nose, and throat > Basics of ENT > Nose and sinuses*

[Original Article Link](/library/e60xPS)

---

## Summary

The nose is the protruding structure at the center of the face that serves as the organ of <u>smell</u> and entrance of the respiratory system. The <u>paranasal sinuses</u> (maxillary, frontal, ethmoidal, <u>sphenoid</u>) are air-filled cavities within the bones of the <u>skull</u> that surround the nasal cavity. The nose and the <u>paranasal sinuses</u> provide resonance to the voice and humidify and warm inhaled air. The nasal cavity consists of a respiratory region, which is lined with ciliated <u>pseudostratified</u> <u>columnar epithelium</u> interspersed with <u>goblet cells</u>, and an olfactory region, which is lined with <u>pseudostratified</u> <u>ciliated columnar epithelium</u> interspersed with olfactory <u>receptor</u> <u>neurons</u>. Olfactory information is communicated to the <u>brain</u> via the <u>olfactory nerve</u> (<u>CN I</u>), which arises from the <u>respiratory epithelium</u>. The olfactory <u>receptor</u> <u>neurons</u> in the <u>respiratory epithelium</u> react with odorants via <u>diffusion</u> of odorant-binding <u>proteins</u>. The signal is carried by olfactory <u>receptor</u> <u>neurons</u>, whose <u>axons</u> bundle in fascicles. These fascicles then pass through the <u>cribriform</u> plate of the <u>ethmoid bone</u> and form the <u>olfactory bulb</u> within the forebrain. From there the signal is transmitted on to the target regions in the <u>brain</u> via the <u>olfactory tract</u>. Unlike other <u>sensory tracts</u>, the <u>olfactory tract</u> bypasses the <u>thalamic nuclei</u> and projects directly into the <u>primary olfactory cortex</u>. Diseases affecting the nose and the <u>paranasal sinuses</u> include <u>nasal polyps</u>, <u>epistaxis</u>, <u>choanal atresia</u>, and <u>sinusitis</u>.

---

## Gross anatomy

### Overview




* The nose contains the human olfactory system, which is responsible for the <u>sense of smell</u>.

* <u>Paranasal sinuses</u>

* Air-filled cavities within the bones of the <u>skull</u> (frontal, <u>ethmoid</u>, <u>sphenoid</u>) and face (<u>maxilla</u>)

* They reduce the weight of the <u>skull</u>, especially of the frontal and <u>facial bones</u>, to facilitate maintenance of the upright head position.

* The nose and <u>paranasal sinuses</u> fulfill the following functions:

* Help provide resonance to the voice

* Warm and humidify air that is inhaled

* Are part of the <u>mucosal</u> <u>immune system</u>

### Paranasal sinuses




| <u>Characteristics of paranasal sinuses</u> |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sinuses | Location | Structures |
| Frontal sinus | <br>* <u>Frontal bone</u><br><br> | <br>* Connects with the <u>middle nasal meatus</u> via the frontonasal duct, which drains into the semilunar hiatus (a semicircular opening on the <u>lateral</u> aspect of the <u>middle nasal meatus</u>)<br><br> |
| Ethmoidal sinus | <br><br>* Ethmoidal labyrinth<br><br>* Between the <u>orbits</u> and the nasal cavity<br><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Ethmoidal air cells</u><br><br>* <u>Anterior</u> <u>ethmoidal air cells</u> (the largest of which is the ethmoid bulla); drain into the <u>middle nasal meatus</u><br><br>* Middle <u>ethmoidal air cells</u>; drain into the <u>middle nasal meatus</u><br><br>* <u>Posterior</u> <u>ethmoidal cells</u>; drain into the <u>superior nasal meatus</u><br><br>* Present at <u>birth</u><br><br><br> |
| Sphenoid sinus | <br>* <u>Sphenoid bone</u><br><br> | <br>* Drains into the <u>sphenoethmoidal recess</u> in the nasal cavity<br><br> |
| Maxillary sinus | <br>* <u>Maxilla</u> (bilateral)<br><br> | <br><br>* Present at <u>birth</u><br><br>* Drains into the <u>middle nasal meatus</u><br><br><br> |

### The nose




#### Bones



* Frontal, <u>ethmoid</u>, <u>maxilla</u>, nasal, palatine, <u>sphenoid</u>, <u>vomer</u>




#### Boundaries




* Roof: composed of the nasal, frontal, <u>cribriform</u> plate (<u>ethmoid</u>), and <u>sphenoid bone</u>

* Floor

* Composed of the <u>maxilla</u> (<u>palatine process</u>) and the <u>palatine bone</u> (horizontal plate)

* Transmits branches of the sphenopalatine <u>artery</u> and the nasopalatine nerve through the <u>incisive foramen</u>

* <u>Medial</u> wall (nasal septum): composed of septal <u>cartilage</u>, the <u>vomer</u>, and the perpendicular plate of the <u>ethmoid bone</u>

* <u>Lateral</u> wall: composed of the <u>nasal bone</u>, <u>lacrimal bone</u>, <u>medial pterygoid</u> plate of the <u>sphenoid bone</u>, perpendicular plate of the <u>palatine bone</u>, frontal process of the <u>maxilla</u>, nasal surface of the <u>maxilla</u>, and the inferior, middle, and <u>superior meatus</u>





![Nasal septum](media/lvfbhc2uneapggbupncwar8p.jpg)

Nasal septum




#### Meatus




| <br>Nasal meatuses and recesses<br> |  |
| --- | --- |
| Meatus | Drainage |
| Superior meatus | <br>* <u>Posterior</u> <u>ethmoidal air cells</u><br><br> |
| Middle meatus | <br><br>* <u>Anterior</u> and middle <u>ethmoidal air cells</u><br><br>* <u>Maxillary sinus</u><br><br>* <u>Frontal sinus</u> (into the infundibulum)<br><br><br> |
| Inferior meatus | <br>* <u>Nasolacrimal duct</u><br><br> |
| Sphenoethmoidal recess | <br>* <u>Sphenoid sinus</u><br><br> |
| Sphenopalatine recess | <br>* <u>Pterygopalatine fossa</u><br><br> |





![Nasal meatuses and recesses](media/tlsn1nbceq4bcyqj9wq6h2p3.jpg)

Nasal meatuses and recesses




#### Vasculature




* <u>Ophthalmic artery</u>: <u>lateral</u> nasal branches of the <u>anterior</u> and <u>posterior</u> ethmoidal <u>arteries</u>

* Maxillary <u>artery</u>

* Posterolateral and posteroseptal branches of the sphenopalatine <u>arteries</u>

* Greater palatine branch of the descending palatine <u>artery</u>

* Facial <u>artery</u>

* Superior labial <u>artery</u>

* <u>Lateral</u> nasal branch





![Arterial supply of the nasal septum](media/vbw4856w32qbe61jnuqhylyw.jpg)

Arterial supply of the nasal septum




> [!NOTE]
> <u>Kiesselbach plexus</u> is formed by the <u>anterior ethmoidal artery</u>, sphenopalatine <u>artery</u>, greater palatine <u>artery</u>, and the septal branch of the superior labial <u>artery</u>.




#### Innervation




* <u>Olfaction</u>: via the <u>olfactory nerve</u> (<u>cranial nerve I</u>), which is responsible for the transmission of olfactory signals from the <u>olfactory epithelium</u> to the <u>brain</u>

* Other sensation

* <u>Pterygopalatine ganglion</u>

* Nasopalatine branch

* <u>Posterior</u>-superior branch

* <u>Posterior</u>-inferior branch

* <u>Anterior</u> and <u>posterior</u> ethmoidal branch of the <u>ophthalmic nerve</u>

* <u>Anterior</u>-superior alveolar branch of the <u>infraorbital nerve</u>

## Microscopic anatomy

### <u>Respiratory epithelium</u>




* Formed by the lower two-thirds of the nasal cavity

* The <u>anterior</u> part of the vestibule in the nasal cavity is lined with keratinized, <u>stratified</u>, <u>squamous epithelium</u>.

* <u>Posterior</u> to the vestibule, the <u>epithelium</u> becomes <u>pseudostratified</u>, <u>ciliated columnar epithelium</u> with <u>goblet cells</u> (<u>respiratory epithelium</u>).

* Contains vibrissae, short and thick <u>hair</u> that filter large particles from inspired air

* The <u>lamina propria</u> is abundantly vascularized.

* Serves to warm, humidify, and clean air that is inhaled





![Respiratory epithelium of the nasal mucosa](media/u8ckr0cuxubr0k690lnum1oc.jpg)

Respiratory epithelium of the nasal mucosa




### <u>Olfactory epithelium</u>




* Found on the roof of the nasal cavity, in the <u>superior nasal meatus</u>, on both sides of the <u>nasal septum</u>

* Lined by tall, <u>pseudostratified</u>, ciliated, <u>columnar epithelium</u>

* Olfactory cells

* Sustentacular and microvillar (supporting) cells

* <u>Basal cells</u>

* The <u>lamina propria</u> contains <u>Bowman glands</u>, <u>fibroblasts</u>, <u>blood vessels</u>, and unmyelinated fibers from the olfactory <u>neurons</u>.

* Olfactory glands (<u>Bowman glands</u>) are tubulo-alveolar glands in the olfactory <u>mucosa</u> that secrete odorant-binding <u>proteins</u>, <u>IgA</u>, <u>amylase</u>, <u>lysozyme</u>

* <u>Bowman glands</u> moisten the nasal <u>mucosa</u> and acts as a solvent for odor molecules.





![Olfactory pathway](media/u6pjvwpmtqmmaeaif20q2bd2.jpg)

Olfactory pathway

## Olfaction (smell)

### Overview




* Molecules are inspired and absorbed by the respiratory region of the nose before reaching the <u>olfactory epithelium</u>.

* <u>Smell</u> is the sensation produced when the <u>olfactory epithelium</u> reacts with dissolved odorant substances.

* Mucus secretion is required for odorant molecules to interact with the <u>olfactory epithelium</u> (aids in dissolving odorants).

* The conscious and unconscious perception of <u>smell</u> takes place in different areas of the <u>brain</u>.

* Conscious perception of <u>smell</u>: orbitofrontal cortex

* Unconscious perception of <u>smell</u>: <u>amygdala</u> (and other structures of the <u>limbic system</u>)

* <u>Smell</u> plays an important role in the formation of <u>memory</u> and emotions.

* <u>Smell</u> aids in <u>gustation</u> (sense of <u>taste</u>).





![Olfactory pathway](media/u6pjvwpmtqmmaeaif20q2bd2.jpg)

Olfactory pathway

![Sensory Transduction: How Our Senses Work](media/small_5dfa14de73fd7.jpg)

Sensory Transduction: How Our Senses Work




### Anatomy of <u>smell</u>




* The olfactory <u>neurons</u> are primarily located in the superior part of the nasal cavity.

* Odorants travel through the <u>superior nasal meatus</u> to reach the <u>olfactory bulb</u>.

* The olfactory system is characterized by direct projections that connect directly to the cortex, bypassing the <u>thalamic nuclei</u> (unlike other sensory systems).





#### Olfactory epithelium




* Olfactory receptor cells

* Primary sensory <u>neurons</u>, bipolar <u>neurons</u> that contain <u>chemoreceptors</u>

* <u>Cilia</u>, dendritic knobs, <u>dendrites</u>, and cell bodies of olfactory cells are contained within the <u>olfactory epithelium</u>.

* The unmyelinated <u>axons</u> of olfactory cells penetrate the fenestrated <u>cribriform</u> plate of the <u>ethmoid bone</u>.

* Odorants react with <u>olfactory receptor cells</u> via <u>diffusion</u> or odorant-binding <u>proteins</u>.

* Sustentacular cells: contain <u>microvilli</u> and secretory granules

* <u>Basal cells</u>: <u>stem cells</u> of the <u>olfactory epithelium</u>





#### Olfactory bulb




* Olfactory glomerulus: <u>neurons</u> with identical olfactory <u>receptors</u> form <u>glomeruli</u> in the <u>olfactory bulb</u>.

* Second <u>neurons</u>

* Tufted cells

* Mitral cells

* Periglomerular cell: inhibit <u>mitral cells</u> and <u>tufted cells</u> laterally → sharper contrast between different smells

* Interneurons

* <u>Granule cells</u>





![Olfactory mucosa and bulb](media/jgp4v9tcqjprp4cwii3hver6.jpg)

Olfactory mucosa and bulb

![Primary and secondary sensory cells](media/sgo29xpm8bdi6936t661eetb.jpg)

Primary and secondary sensory cells




#### <u>Smell</u> pathways




Several areas of the <u>brain</u> are associated with the <u>sense of smell</u>, including: the <u>anterior olfactory nucleus</u>, <u>amygdala</u>, piriform cortex, <u>entorhinal cortex</u>, and olfactory tubercle.




| Overview of <u>smell</u> pathways |  |
| --- | --- |
| Structure | Characteristics |
| <br>Olfactory tract <br> | <br><br>* Contains the <u>anterior olfactory nucleus</u><br><br>* Formed by the <u>axons</u> of <u>mitral cells</u><br><br>* <u>Medial</u> <u>olfactory tract</u>: <u>ipsilateral</u> projection to the <u>anterior olfactory nucleus</u><br><br>* <u>Lateral</u> <u>olfactory tract</u>: projections <u>synapse</u> in third-order <u>neurons</u> located in the <u>entorhinal cortex</u> (<u>secondary olfactory cortex</u>) and <u>amygdaloid nucleus</u><br><br>* <u>Contralateral</u> projections occurs via the <u>anterior</u> commissure<br><br>* Third-order <u>neurons</u> project to the <u>dorsomedial nucleus</u> (in the <u>thalamus</u>), <u>basal forebrain</u>, and <u>limbic system</u><br><br><br> |
| Primary olfactory cortex | <br>* Formed by:<br><br>* The piriform cortex: encompasses the <u>olfactory tract</u>, <u>anterior</u> part of the parahippocampal <u>gyrus</u>, and the <u>uncus</u><br><br>* The prepiriform and the periamygdaloid areas of the <u>temporal lobe</u>.<br><br>* Receives input from the <u>lateral</u> <u>olfactory tract</u><br><br>* Projects into the <u>dorsomedial nucleus</u> (in the <u>thalamus</u>), <u>hippocampus</u>, and <u>hypothalamus</u><br><br> |
| Secondary olfactory cortex | <br>* Formed by the <u>entorhinal cortex</u> and <u>insula</u>.<br><br> |
| Olfactory nuclei | <br><br>* Anterior olfactory nucleus<br><br>* Located within the <u>olfactory tract</u><br><br>* Receives input from <u>mitral cell</u> fibers via the <u>medial</u> <u>olfactory tract</u><br><br>* Projects to the <u>contralateral</u> <u>olfactory bulb</u> via the <u>anterior</u> commissure<br><br>* <u>Dorsomedial nucleus</u> (in the <u>thalamus</u>)<br>* Projects to the orbitofrontal cortex (area for conscious perception of <u>smell</u>)<br><br>* <u>Amygdaloid nucleus</u><br><br>* Receives input from the <u>lateral</u> <u>olfactory tract</u><br><br>* Projects to the mediodorsal <u>nucleus</u> (in the <u>thalamus</u>)<br><br><br> |

## Embryology

* Development of the nose starts during the 3<sup>rd</sup> week of <u>embryogenesis</u>.

* The <u>olfactory nerve</u> derives from paired ectodermal nasal (olfactory) placodes.

* The <u>epithelium</u> of the nose and <u>paranasal sinuses</u> derives from <u>surface ectoderm</u>.

* The bones of the nose and <u>paranasal sinuses</u> derive from <u>mesoderm</u>.
